Fit an optimal Variable Length Markov Chain with Covariates (COVLMC)

Source: R/covlmc_tune.R
tune_covlmc.Rd

This function fits a Variable Length Markov Chain with Covariates (COVLMC) to a discrete time series coupled with a time series of covariates by optimising an information criterion (BIC or AIC).

Usage

tune_covlmc(
  x,
  covariate,
  criterion = c("BIC", "AIC"),
  initial = c("truncated", "specific", "extended"),
  alpha_init = NULL,
  min_size = 5,
  max_depth = 100,
  verbose = 0,
  save = c("best", "initial", "all"),
  trimming = c("full", "partial", "none"),
  best_trimming = c("none", "partial", "full"),
  control = covlmc_control()
)

Arguments

x

an object that can be interpreted as a discrete time series: a numeric, character, factor or logical vector, or a dts object (see dts()). Its state space must contain at least two states.

covariate

a data frame of covariates.

criterion

criterion used to select the best model. Either "BIC" (default) or "AIC" (see details).

initial

specifies the likelihood function, more precisely the way the first few observations for which contexts cannot be calculated are integrated in the likelihood. Defaults to "truncated". See loglikelihood() for details.

alpha_init

if non NULL, used as the initial cut off parameter (in quantile scale, in (0,1]) to build the initial COVLMC. The default NULL corresponds to 0.5 (see details).

min_size

number >= 1 (default: 5). Tune the minimum number of observations for a context in the growing phase of the context tree (see covlmc() for details).

max_depth

integer >= 0 (default: 100). Longest context considered in growing phase of the initial context tree (see details).

verbose

integer >= 0 (default: 0). Verbosity level of the pruning process. The progress is reported with message(), which can be silenced with suppressMessages().

save

specifies which models are saved during the pruning process. The default value "best" asks the function to keep only the best model according to the criterion. When save="initial" the function keeps in addition the initial (complex) model which is then pruned during the selection process. When save="all", the function returns all the models considered during the selection process. See details for memory occupation.

trimming

specifies the type of trimming used when saving the intermediate models: "full" (default), "partial" or "none" (see the Memory occupation section).

best_trimming

specifies the type of trimming used when saving the best model and the initial one: "none" (default), "partial" or "full" (see the Memory occupation section).

control

a list with control parameters used to fit the models, see covlmc_control().

Value

an object of class tune_covlmc, a list with the following components:

  • best_model: the optimal COVLMC

  • criterion: the criterion used to select the optimal COVLMC

  • initial: the likelihood function used to select the optimal COVLMC

  • results: a data frame with details about the pruning process, with one row per model and the columns alpha, depth, nb_contexts, loglikelihood, cov_depth, AIC and BIC

  • saved_models: a list of intermediate COVLMCs if save="initial" or save="all". It contains an initial component with the large COVLMC obtained first and, when save="all", an all component with a list of all the other COVLMCs obtained by pruning the initial one.

Details

This function automates the process of fitting a large COVLMC to a discrete time series with covlmc() and of pruning the tree (with cutoff() and prune()) to get an optimal model with respect to an information criterion. To avoid missing long-term dependencies, the function uses the max_depth parameter as an initial guess but then relies on an automatic increase of the value to make sure the initial context tree is only limited by the min_size parameter. The initial value of the alpha parameter of covlmc() is also set to a conservative value (0.5) to avoid prior simplification of the context tree. This can be overridden by setting the alpha_init parameter to a more adapted value.

Once the initial COVLMC is obtained, the cutoff() and prune() functions are used to build all the COVLMC models that could be generated using smaller values of the alpha parameter. The best model is selected from this collection, including the initial complex tree, as the one that minimises the chosen information criterion.

Memory occupation

covlmc objects tend to be large and saving all the models during the search for the optimal model can lead to an unreasonable use of memory. To avoid this problem, intermediate models are kept only in trimmed form using trim.covlmc() with keep_model=FALSE. Both the initial model and the best one are saved untrimmed. This default behaviour corresponds to trimming="full". Setting trimming="partial" asks the function to use keep_model=TRUE in trim.covlmc() for intermediate models. Finally, trimming="none" turns off trimming, which is discouraged except for small data sets.

In parallel processing contexts (e.g. using foreach::%dopar%), the results are serialised to be sent back to the main process: as the logistic models keep the data used to fit them (including in the environments attached to their formulas), this can be costly. It is highly recommended to trim all saved models, including the best one and the initial one. This can be done via the best_trimming parameter whose possible values are identical to the ones of trimming.

See also

covlmc(), cutoff() and prune()

Examples

pc <- powerconsumption[powerconsumption$week %in% 6:7, ]
rdts <- cut(pc$active_power, breaks = c(0, quantile(pc$active_power, probs = c(0.5, 1))))
rdts_cov <- data.frame(day_night = (pc$hour >= 7 & pc$hour <= 17))
rdts_best_model_tune <- tune_covlmc(rdts, rdts_cov)
rdts_best_model_tune
#> VLMC with covariates context tree on (0,1.26], (1.26,6.48] 
#>  cutoff in quantile scale: 0.001838
#>  Number of contexts: 6 
#>  Maximum context length: 4 
#>  Selected by BIC (1103.29) with likelihood function "truncated" (-525.026)
draw(as_covlmc(rdts_best_model_tune))
#> ▪
#> ├─ (0,1.26]
#> │  ├─ (0,1.26] (0.931, 0.06897)
#> │  └─ (1.26,6.48] (0.8205, 0.1795)
#> └─ (1.26,6.48]
#>    ├─ (0,1.26] (0.1538, 0.8462)
#>    └─ (1.26,6.48]
#>       ├─ (0,1.26] (0.1667, 0.8333)
#>       └─ (1.26,6.48]
#>          ├─ (0,1.26] ([ 0.47 • 2.862 ])
#>          └─ (1.26,6.48] (0.05439, 0.9456)
## details of the pruning process
rdts_best_model_tune$results

## selection with the AIC, keeping all the (trimmed) intermediate models
rdts_aic_tune <- tune_covlmc(rdts, rdts_cov, criterion = "AIC", save = "all")
length(rdts_aic_tune$saved_models$all)
#> [1] 13
